summary_paragraph: A 70-year-old woman with a history of CAD s/p CABG, hypothyroidism, anxiety, and osteoporosis was admitted for abdominal heaviness concerning for an anginal equivalent. Evaluation revealed negative troponins, no EKG changes indicating ischemia, and a benign abdominal exam. The symptom resolved and was attributed to stress and possible gastritis from high-dose aspirin without PPI coverage. She was restarted on omeprazole and transitioned to 81 mg aspirin daily. Her anxiety, exacerbated by a verbally abusive husband and family stressors, was addressed with social work and continuation of doxepin, with a recommendation to consider an SSRI. Macrocytic anemia and thrombocytopenia were noted, with borderline low ferritin; she was discharged on thiamine and folic acid with a recommendation for outpatient hematology evaluation. She remained stable, with improved labs and no cardiac or respiratory complications, and was discharged home with follow-up plans.
